bear_case: Counter-argument: The BTC and SPCX divergence during the June 18 Iran-deal rally is the most diagnostic signal of the week — and it is bearish for high-duration risk assets. On a session where Nasdaq gained +1.91% and Russell 2000 gained +2.12%, Bitcoin fell -2.41% and SPCX fell through its $185 daily close stop (closing $174.90, -8.82%). Two of the three active long positions in this portfolio failed to participate in a confirmed geopolitical relief rally. The Warsh hawkish regime — nine hike dots, 3.8% median, no forward guidance — is selectively repricing the highest-duration risk assets even as index-level prints recover. DXY at 100.15 on June 18 close despite Brent -5% is the clearest signal: the Fed's 80-basis-point tightening signal is overriding the Iran disinflation impulse. If DXY fails to break below 99.00 on Monday June 22 — and current momentum (dollar holding above 100 through the deal signing) suggests it may not — the BUY upgrade does not activate and HOLD becomes a ceiling, not a temporary regime. The May PCE print on June 25 (estimated at 4.1% YoY) could simultaneously push the 30Y above the 5.00% trigger and spike VIX above 18, collapsing both cleared gates in a single session and forcing a full STEP_ASIDE. Invalidation: if SPX breaks below 7,460 on Monday June 22 open, the call reverts to STEP_ASIDE immediately regardless of DXY.
